Zig 0.17 Upgrade Comparison > Zig 0.17 vs 0.14.1: Measured Comparison

Zig 0.17 vs 0.14.1: Measured Comparison (2026-10-13)

The question: after sci upgraded the compiler from Zig 0.14.1 to 0.17, are the generated programs faster or slower? This page re-measures all reproducible peers with the sa built by 0.17, alongside this site's existing 0.14.1 data. The conclusion up front: the same performance tier, with no systematic regression — the backend is LLVM 14 in both cases, and a diff confirms the JS emitter differs only at the comment level; the observed fluctuations within ±2x are attributed to differences in the machines' memory subsystems (see the §5 calibration), unrelated to the toolchain version. There are also two real 0.17 migration fixes (§6), one of which — the native case — would have made things 44x slower if left unfixed.

1. Method and Environment

  • The 0.17 column: the zig-out/bin/sa (Debug) built by sci@0.17 (after this migration), an Intel Xeon 2.20GHz container, node v20.19.0, bun 1.4.3, the llvm-14-dev system libraries.
  • The 0.14.1 column: this site's existing records (the sections of 04_cli/13_bun_peer.html and related commit information), from the author's own machine, bun 1.4.3 (the mitata criteria agree, see §5). The 0.14 compiler was not rebuilt, so cross-machine comparison of absolute values looks only at the tier.
  • Each peer was run 3 times; the table gives the median; the slope criteria follow this site's convention (a two-point difference over 500→5000 rounds, eliminating fixed startup/fill costs).
  • Correctness: all peers' output checksums agree with the 0.14.1 records (PEER32/PEER/B64/HEX/ESC/FIND/FINDM/B64N/B64BIG/HEXN OK).

Also measured (under the current files' criteria, whose workloads are not exactly the same as the old records', see §7): esc (100 rounds) node ~120ms / bun ~73ms ESC OK; findn (2000 rounds) node ~230ms / bun ~199ms FIND OK. Reading: compute-dense work (rw/micro-operations) is level to slightly faster on this machine, while bandwidth-dense work (64KB host-codec) is about 1.7–2x slower on this machine — the two classes point in opposite directions, which is exactly the fingerprint of a machine memory-subsystem difference, not a toolchain effect (for the emitter diff, see §5).

5. Machine Calibration and Emitter Consistency Evidence

  • Re-measuring the original mitata problems on this machine with the same bun 1.4.3 version: readUInt8 2.51µs (record 3.159µs, 0.79x), readInt32LE 2.70µs (record 3.286µs, 0.82x) — this machine's engine micro-operations are about 1.25x faster. Bandwidth-type work (64KB host-codec) is conversely about 2x slower: the compute vs bandwidth subsystems point in opposite directions, which is the typical fingerprint of a cross-machine comparison, unrelated to the toolchain.
  • git diff main 0.17 -- src/emit_js.zig: only mechanical migration changes (ArrayList→Managed, the Io API) + one sext helper (Math.trunc→|0, faster); the host-codec bridge (sa_b64dec/sa_hexdec) emission is byte-for-byte identical (only a one-line comment difference). The generated JS is substantively the same, so the performance differences do not come from the emitter.
  • The backend is LLVM 14 in both cases (llvm-14-dev, with llvm-include-dir unchanged), and the native code generation path is the same.

6. Two Real 0.17 Fixes (Without Them the Comparison Could Not Be Made)

  • UBSan's default set expanded: Zig 0.17's zig cc has a default sanitizer set far larger than 0.14's, so libsa_std.a and user .bc files get __ubsan_handle_* injected; native glibc linking without a ubsan runtime then reports undefined symbols (the simd peers were all wiped out), and the checking overhead slowed native rw from 4ms to 176ms (44x). Fix: add -fno-sanitize=all at three C shims in build.zig plus three argv spots in zigcc.zig, restoring the 0.14 behavior; the archive has been verified to have zero ubsan references.
  • The wasm entry contract: the 0.17 toolchain's wasi-libc removed the weak default __main_argc_argv (0.14 called main indirectly through it), so the old emission's main was referenced by nobody and linked into an unreachable stub. Fix: under wasm_compat, rename the entry to __main_argc_argv (emit_llvm_llvmc_shim.c); hello/the whole matrix are restored.

7. Criteria Differences and an Honesty Statement

  • esc/find used different round counts from the old records (current files: esc 100 rounds / findn 2000 rounds; old records: esc 200 rounds / find 2500×4), so absolute values are not directly comparable; only the tier and correctness are.
  • The old hex native record (3.1ms) came from a pure-table peer; the current peer_hex.sa is the JS host-codec version (with no native symbols, by design); native hex re-establishes its baseline with peer_hexn20000.
  • b64nbig's single-run 19ms includes process startup + verification; when comparing against the slope criteria (1.13ns/B) the fixed cost should be deducted.
  • The compiler itself is a Debug build; the program side uniformly uses --release-fast (the same criteria as §14).
  • Summary verdict: 0.17 and 0.14.1 are in the same tier, with no systematic regression; correctness (all checksums) is completely identical.

7. Plugin Migration Status (2026-10-19)

Besides sci itself, the 0.17 branches of all SA plugin repositories have also been migrated to Zig 0.17: sax, react, mui, vite, tui, wgpu, 3dengines (including 24 3D sub-plugins), vm, sla, deno, node, bun, pkg, http-client, http-server, db, bc2sa. Every repository builds with Zig 0.17, passes the Zig unit tests, and passes installation verification via SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa plugin install --dev; sci uses the main branch (including the PIC object fix). The plugin-side changes concentrate on std.Io / sio adaptation, std.array_list.Managed, dupeSentinel, the removed usingnamespace, and Zig 0.17 behavior changes such as export declarations needing an explicit reference before they enter the dynamic library symbol table. See the Plugin Reference overview for details.

Sources: medians of three runs on this machine for sci@0.17; the 0.14.1 column is quoted from this site's 04_cli/13_bun_peer.html and related commit records; mitata calibration: re-measured with the same bun 1.4.3 version.
